set.typical_award_size: Three-year BHSA Integrated Plan (FY 2026/27 to 2028/29), approved by the Board of Supervisors June 2, 2026 (Resolution 26-231); staff report estimates BHSA expenditures of $27,502,891 over three years. Housing Interventions base allocation is 30 percent: $2,460,099 (FY 26/27), $2,596,276 (FY 27/28) and $2,752,206 (FY 28/29), half for chronic homelessness. The County will use housing funds for rental subsidies (about 200 people a year, 103 in permanent supportive housing and 97 in interim hotel or motel stays), project-based and tenant-based, plus outreach and engagement; it will not use BHSA for capital development (0 of the allowed 25 percent). BHSA-funded PSH beds grew from 20 (2019) to 94 (2026), with about 24 Homekey+ units coming.
set.layering_notes: Classified grant: the BHSA plan funds rental subsidies for permanent supportive housing (project-based and tenant-based), not capital. Nevada County's Housing and Community Services Department (HCS) administers the Western Nevada County Regional Housing Trust Fund, PLHA, state HOME and CDBG awards and the Down Payment Assistance Program; the Behavioral Health Department holds Homekey+, BHSA and the Truckee Navigation Center; HHAP is administered by the Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras (CoC CA-531); the Regional Housing Authority supplies vouchers. BHSA rental assistance is used where a voucher is not available, so a PSH developer should plan on BHSA as an operating or rental subsidy source for a handful of units, not as gap capital. Capital has come from BHBH, BHCIP, ERF and Homekey+ instead. Staff report and resolution are on Legistar (nevco matter SR 26-0325).

set.affordability_requirement: Property use restricted to lower income households by a recorded deed restriction or regulatory agreement; property must receive state or federal LIHTC or government financing (or 90 percent or more of tenants qualify); owner needs a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate, and LP owners a Supplemental Clearance Certificate.
